svg.title: Past search schematic 06: entry 25, “the cave of the pillar with the two entrances”: the candidates and the digs
svg.text: Past searches 06 — entry 25, “the cave of the pillar with the two entrances”: the candidates and the digs
Not to scale, except the depth tracks (0–3 m). Rows are candidate caves named in the repo; none is identified with entry 25. Red = the text.
The text's clues against each candidate cave
Atlas: entry 25 is “possible only”, confidence low, at the level of the Kh. Qumran district; no feature is identified.
Rows: the three caves the repo compares with entry 25 (question R02), and the cave Jones dug in 1992 (S14). All are candidates.
a smaller cave just N of
† Same cave as Bar-Adon's Twin Cave: the ledger joins S09 and S15 by seasons and team (inference). Bearings and threshold: see the side panel.
The digs at each candidate: who, when, what, how deep, result
Blue bar = dug, from today's surface; dashed = no figure. Ochre dashed = surveyed or measured, not dug. Red band = the text's 3 cubits, counted from the ancient
northern threshold, which no report gives; so a bar and the band are not on the same datum.
1971 trial cut in the north cave;
pottery of many periods, some Roman;
a passage cut into the column
small amounts of pottery and flint;
no sherds or other indicative material:
at the mouth: debris over a

The text, and what stays open
“[In] the cave of the pillar with the two [en]trances, facing
east, [at] the northern entrance, dig three [cu]bits: there is a
jar, in it one scroll; under it 42 talents.”
One arrangement the text allows: not a real cave, not to scale
No jar with a scroll, and no silver, is reported at any of them.
Twin Cave: a deposit several metres thick; pottery of many
periods, some with late Second Temple parallels; 1986: nothing
IV/11: Iron Age, Hellenistic/Roman finds. IV/17: Hellenistic
finds; Sion dates its use to the 2nd–1st c. BCE.
A northern threshold of the right period, with a level, at any
candidate: three cubits has no starting point.
True bearings of any mouth (IV/17's ≈ 119–123° are Plan 5
A measured plan of Twin Cave (Fig. B1 is a photograph), or when
any pillar or mouth was cut.
Frozen 9 Oct 2026: “east” = 45°–135° for a mouth's facing. A
FAIL at IV/17's mouths would remove 3 of 6 entry-25 model
classes; a PASS, none. Nothing scored yet.
Awaited: Dadon's L-656 field file (threshold levels, wall
Twin Cave: no cave item found in Gnazim 717 (Bar-Adon's papers).
Not entry-25 candidates on this sheet
Cave 13 (S13, 1988): Patrich with Jones's volunteers; one
east-facing opening; a juglet of oil.
Allegro's Golden Gate, Jerusalem (1960 p. 104): read as a gate,
not a cave; no fieldwork of his.
Translation VI 1–6; atlas entry 25; ledger S09, S10, S13–S15, S20 (searches.csv, README); Bar-Adon,
ʿAtiqot Heb. Ser. 9 (1989) pp. [15]–17; ESI 6 pp. 69–70; Feig and Sion, ʿAtiqot 41 (2002) pp. 61–64,
Allegro 1960 p. 104; the repo notes named in the script.
A matrix, not a map: not to scale, except the depth tracks (0–3 m). Cells follow the repo's notes;
ledger fields are checked at build. Red sketch: schematic, after the text.
Twin Cave and IV/17 each have a published pillar between two mouths; IV/11 has an inner pillar and
one recorded opening. The digs give no depth, or a depth from today's surface; none records a period
northern threshold to count three cubits from.
Which cave, if any, is the scroll's: all four are candidates. If three cubits is a depth, a dig tests
the clue only when measured from the period threshold. Positions: Twin Cave is near Kh. Qumran; IV/11
and IV/17 are in the Jebel Abu Saraj cliff.
